author: Angelica Cheyenne
title: Colbert confronts Democratic governor on 'crazy' gerrymandering in Texas controversy - NewsBreak
text: On his late-night CBS show , Stephen Colbert didn't miss the chance to call out Democratic Illinois Governor JB Pritzker during Tuesday's broadcast. In the middle of the episode, Stephen whipped out a congressional map of Illinois while Governor Pritzker was on screen, pointing out a peculiarly shaped district that he likened to "the stinger on a scorpion." By doing so, Stephen highlighted the extent of gerrymandering in the Prairie State, especially after several Texas Democratic lawmakers reportedly protested redistricting in their state by escaping to Illinois and New York , as per the New York Post. "If you are considering doing a little more redrawing in Illinois, you already have some crazy districts in Illinois," Stephen quipped to the governor. READ MORE: Amy Bradley's brother reveals major update in the case after Netflix documentary READ MORE: New Amy Bradley leads emerge following Netflix documentary 27 years later "Take a look at this. Look at [District] 17 here. It does that, then it comes up here and it sneaks around there and goes all the way up here, and then goes right over there like that. And look at this one, kind of goes whoop up there," the host elaborated. Governor Pritzker stood his ground when talking about potentially redrawing district lines to benefit Democratic congressional hopefuls. "It's possible," the governor, who is rumored to have presidential ambitions for 2028, responded when questioned if Illinois might retaliate against Texas' redistricting with a similar tactic. "As I've said, everything's on the table," Governor JB declared. "Look, we've got to fight fire with fire. They've frankly tossed the rulebook out. And they're just acting in an unconstitutional fashion." The practice of manipulating congressional districts for political advantage, known as gerrymandering, dates back centuries. The term itself originated in 1812 when Massachusetts Democratic-Republican Gov. Elbridge Gerry approved a partisan redistricting plan for the United States Senate districts. During a conversation, Stephen inquired, "Is this common for all states to do?" To which the Illinois governor responded with a quip: "We handed it over to a kindergarten class and let them decide,". Stephen then questioned, "That's the nonpartisan group that does this?" prompting JB to confirm, "That's our independent commission, yeah." Pressing further, Stephen asked, "So because all states, to a certain extent, do this, why is what Texas doing particularly egregious in this case?" JB elaborated, "What the Republicans are trying to do in the - Texas Republicans frankly, at the behest of Donald Trump are doing it mid-decade. That is extraordinarily rare." Stephen highlighted, "That's a good point because I think he literally called them or wrote them and said, 'Hey, I need five seats, go redraw this.'" Currently, Illinois sends 17 members to the House, with only three being Republicans. Last year, President Donald Trump secured nearly 44% of the Illinois vote in the presidential election, indicating that a balanced map would have included seven GOP House members.
